Overview of M ATH A RENA benchmarks newly introduced in this paper.
Apex Shortlist is a broader companion set of difficult competition problems for the same olympiad-level high-school audience.
We focused on competitions held in 2025, drawing primarily from the AoPS community as well as a range of primary sources.
If at least one model fails on at least one attempt, the problem is included in Apex Shortlist.
This process yielded 12 Apex problems and 48 Apex Shortlist problems.
These problems were extracted from official sources and tested against frontier models available at the time of construction (August 2025) to ensure difficulty.
Problems unsolved by all tested models were included in the Apex benchmark, while those unsolved by at least one tested model were placed in the Apex Shortlist.
To obtain more reliable estimates, we run each model four times on each benchmark and average the resulting scores.
We report 95% confidence intervals for all model scores using the normal approximation,
Final-answer benchmarks consist of questions with a single unambiguous answer, which makes fully automatic evaluation possible.
we use an LLM judge to evaluate answer correctness and manually review all cases in which the judge disagrees with the parser, which occurs for fewer than 1% of answers.

Final-answer competitions are saturated.
On final-answer benchmarks such as AIME and HMMT, top models now achieve near-perfect performance, with GPT-5.5 reaching 97% on both.
In contrast, both Apex and Apex Shortlist still have some limited headroom, with state-of-the-art performance at 80% and 94%, respectively.
Models are required to output their final answer in a boxed LATEX environment (e.g., \boxed{2}) to make parsing easier for our evaluation code.
In particular, the model frequently reached its maximum token limit, which we could not increase because the API allowed at most 128k tokens.
at the 95% level, its coverage is 95.99%, compared with 98.83% for Wilson, 87.75% for the question plug-in interval, 98.54% for the Jeffreys-smoothed variant, and 96.80% for the question-SD interval.

MathArena evaluates LLMs on recent math competitions, olympiads, and research problems.

Each model runs four times on each problem.
The leaderboards show average scores and the average cost of a single run on one problem, in USD.
